title: micro-ROS Teleoperation
description: Integrate Raspberry Pi Pico W with ROS2 ecosystem using micro-ROS to control robots remotely.
objectives: Understand micro-ROS architecture and ROS2 integration
Create publishers and subscribers on Pico W
Implement robot teleoperation with velocity commands
Monitor topics and debug with ROS2 tools

connections: L298N GND → Battery GND + Pico GND
warnings: NEVER connect battery directly to Pico (only through L298N)
Always share GND between all components
Verify motor polarity before final assembly
Use external battery for motors, USB only for Pico

theory.microros: micro-ROS brings ROS2 to microcontrollers. Uses XRCE-DDS protocol to communicate with ROS2 via agent running on PC.
theory.agent: micro-ROS agent acts as bridge between Pico W and ROS2. Receives XRCE-DDS messages and translates to DDS (ROS2 standard).
theory.cmdvel: geometry_msgs/Twist is standard message for velocity commands. Contains linear (x,y,z) and angular (x,y,z) velocities. Differential robots use linear.x (forward) and angular.z (rotation).
theory.qos: Quality of Service defines communication reliability. For teleoperation: RELIABLE for critical commands, BEST_EFFORT for high-frequency data (sensors).

steps.title: Install micro-ROS Agent
steps.description: Set up development environment on PC
details: Create agent: ros2 run micro_ros_setup create_agent_ws.sh
Build agent: ros2 run micro_ros_setup build_agent.sh
Test: ros2 run micro_ros_agent micro_ros_agent udp4 --port 8888

steps.title: Configure Pico W with micro-ROS
details: Flash firmware to Pico W using Thonny or esptool
Configure agent IP (PC IP address on WiFi network)
Connect to WiFi first, then initialize micro-ROS

steps.title: Create Twist Subscriber
details: Convert to differential drive: left = linear.x - angular.z, right = linear.x + angular.z
Map to PWM range (0-255) and apply to motors

steps.title: Test with teleop_twist_keyboard
details: Run agent: ros2 run micro_ros_agent micro_ros_agent udp4 --port 8888
New terminal: ros2 run teleop_twist_keyboard teleop_twist_keyboard
Verify robot moves according to commands

steps.title: Add Odometry Publisher
details: If no encoders: publish commanded velocities
Visualize in RViz2: ros2 run rviz2 rviz2

bipesProject.description: BIPES project with micro-ROS configured for differential robot. Includes Twist subscriber, motor control and odometry publisher.

troubleshooting.problem: Pico W doesn't connect to agent
solutions: Verify PC and Pico W are on same WiFi network
Check agent IP address is correct (use ifconfig on PC)
Confirm agent is running: ros2 run micro_ros_agent...
Test connectivity: ping [PICO_IP] from PC
Check firewall rules (UDP port 8888 must be open)
Verify battery is charged (minimum 6V)
Check motor connections to L298N
Test motors individually with Digital Write
Confirm PWM signals are being generated (use oscilloscope or LED)
Verify differential drive calculations are correct
Check topic name matches exactly (case-sensitive)
Verify message type is correct: ros2 topic info /cmd_vel
List active topics: ros2 topic list
Echo topic: ros2 topic echo /cmd_vel
Restart agent and Pico W
Reduce maximum velocity in teleop (x/X keys)
Add smoothing/filtering to velocity commands
Implement acceleration limits (rate limiter)
Check motor polarity (one motor might be inverted)
Verify WiFi latency isn't too high (ping test)

challenges.title: Emergency Stop Service
challenges.description: Implement ROS2 service /emergency_stop that immediately stops motors. Call with: ros2 service call /emergency_stop std_srvs/srv/Trigger

challenges.title: Sensor Data Fusion
challenges.description: Add ultrasonic sensor, publish to /scan (sensor_msgs/LaserScan), implement obstacle avoidance that overrides teleop commands when object is too close.

challenges.title: Autonomous Navigation with Nav2
challenges.description: Integrate robot with Nav2 stack. Add IMU and encoders for accurate odometry, create map with SLAM, implement navigation to waypoints using Nav2 action server.
